ticket.title: plan blueprints can be orphaned or point at files that do not exist, and no command notices
ticket.description:
Measured 2026-11-10 while reminting every member store (GB-347). Plan blueprints and the tickets that name them are not checked against each other, so a store can hold a plan nobody owns and a ticket can point at a file that does not exist - and no command says so.  chalkline: the blueprint has no owning ticket (no GB-18 in that store); CH-1 and CH-2 report plan_file_path .gaugeblock/storypole/plans/CH-1.md and CH-2.md, and neither file exists. The pointers were dangling before the remint as CH-1.md and CH-2.md and are still dangling after it.  benchwork: the blueprint and the blueprint have no owning ticket.  storypole: the blueprint has no owning ticket.  remint cannot fix this by design - it renames a blueprint when a ticket owns the key, and there is nothing to rename an orphan after - so the orphans survive a migration that is otherwise exhaustive. The check that would catch it is cheap: for every store, name each plan file with no owning ticket and each plan_file_path that resolves to nothing. `ledger-verify` is the natural home, alongside the structural ledger checks it already performs.

CHECK IMPLEMENTED 2026-11-10, AND IT FOUND MORE THAN THIS TICKET ASSUMED.

`storypole ledger-verify` now audits plans against tickets as well as ledgers against replays:
  orphan    <store>/plans/<KEY>.md has no owning ticket
  dangling  <store>/<TICKET> -> plans/<KEY>.md, where that file does not exist

MEASURED on the suite after the remint:
  59 orphan blueprints, 50 dangling pointers.
  46 of the orphans sit in the ROOT store's plans directory, named for GB-* keys that are now member tickets
  (the blueprint, the blueprint, the blueprint ...). The dangling pointers are the other end of the same files:
  a member ticket pointing at `.gaugeblock/storypole/plans/<KEY>.md` inside ITS OWN repository.

ROOT CAUSE, and it is not the remint. Blueprints were written to the canonical root plans directory while the
tickets were distributed into members, and the pointer was written repository-relative, so it never resolved in
the member that owns the ticket. Verified rather than assumed: outfeed OF-26 pointed at the blueprint before
the remint and that file did not exist in outfeed then either; the same holds for OF-8, OF-9, SH-4 and RB-4.

THE REMEDY IS EXACT. Using the remint record, every member-side dangling pointer resolves to a blueprint in the root
plans directory under the ticket's PRE-REMINT key: 47 checked, 47 matched, 0 unmatched.
  benchwork BW-16 -> the blueprint exists at the root, so the file belongs at benchwork/plans/BW-16.md
Moving each blueprint to its owner and naming it for the ticket's current key would clear both sides at once - the
orphan disappears because the file left, and the dangling pointer becomes valid because the file arrived where the
pointer already looks. That is a write pass, so it needs a verb with a dry run, the same as every other migration
here; it is not implemented in this change.

NOT GATED, DELIBERATELY. `ledger-verify` reports these and does not fail on them. Resolving is a decision - move the
blueprint, or clear a pointer whose document is already inline in the ticket as `design_markdown` - and a check that
guessed would be worse than one that asks. It also must not block eleven repositories' verification chains on data
nobody has judged yet. The findings are in `--json` under `plans` for anything that wants to gate on them later.

Tests: an orphan blueprint and a dangling pointer are both reported; a plan file that exists is clean.

PLACED 2026-11-10 — `storypole plan collect`, and what it could not place.

  `storypole plan collect`          reports the moves
  `storypole plan collect --apply`  moves them

Measured on the suite: 47 blueprints moved, dangling pointers 50 -> 0, orphan blueprints 59 -> 12. Each move is
verified by re-reading the store afterwards and requiring the pointer to resolve.

THE DESTINATION NEEDED NO JUDGEMENT. The pointer already names the ticket's current key inside the ticket's own store,
so putting the file there makes the pointer true as it stands - no ticket was rewritten to make a move work. The SOURCE
needed one lookup: the file on disk carries the key the ticket had before its remint, which the store's remint record
supplies by uuid. That record, written for GB-347, is what made this a mechanical pass instead of archaeology.

IT REFUSED ONE CASE, DELIBERATELY. Three tickets (GB-17, GB-18, GB-36) still point at the pre-GB-344 `.storypole/plans/`
layout. Moving their blueprints to satisfy those pointers would have resurrected the legacy store directory the migration
removed - the exact failure SP-37 was filed for. They were reported as "a pointer to correct, not a file to move", and
then corrected by re-attaching the same blueprint with `plan set`, which writes the canonical path and records it in a
`plan_updated` event rather than editing a file nothing replays.

WHAT IS LEFT IS 12 ORPHAN BLUEPRINTS, and they need a decision this pass cannot supply:
  benchwork/plans/GB-17.md, GB-46.md    chalkline/plans/GB-18.md    storypole/plans/GB-36.md
  plans/OF-23.md, JN-9.md, BW-3.md, BW-6.md, OF-2.md, GB-48.md, GB-55.md, SP-6.md
Each is named for a key no ticket in that store holds, and no ticket points at it either - so neither end of the
relationship exists. They are somebody's design document with no owner: deleting them destroys work, and adopting one
onto a ticket by filename alone is a guess. Reported by `ledger-verify` on every run until a person decides.

ORPHANS RESOLVED 2026-11-10 — every remaining blueprint had an owner; none needed a judgement call after all.

The 12 were two different problems, and the blueprints named their own ticket in the first line (a line of the form `# <KEY>: <title>`), which
is the evidence that resolved them:

  TEN WERE DUPLICATES. Resolved through the remint record, each was byte-identical to a blueprint already owned and
  pointed at elsewhere: root plans/BW-3.md and plans/BW-6.md to benchwork's plans/BW-3.md and plans/BW-6.md;
  plans/OF-2.md, plans/GB-48.md and plans/GB-55.md to outfeed's plans/OF-2.md, OF-3.md and OF-6.md; plans/SP-6.md to
  storypole's plans/SP-6.md. The other four were the mirror image - copies sitting in member stores of blueprints owned by
  the harness (benchwork/plans/GB-17.md, benchwork/plans/GB-46.md, chalkline/plans/GB-18.md, storypole/plans/GB-36.md).
  Identical bytes prove no content is lost by keeping one, and the copy removed is always the one whose store does not
  own the ticket.

  TWO WERE UNATTACHED WORK. The two that named tickets alive today - outfeed's OF-23 and joiner's JN-9 - had no plan
  at all - not a stale pointer, an unwritten one. They were adopted with `plan set`, which writes the blueprint into the
  owning store and records it as a `plan_updated` event, so replay serves it; the root copies then became duplicates and
  were removed with the rest.

  `ledger-verify` now reports 0 orphans and 0 dangling pointers. Measured before this work: 59 and 50.

What made the call safe was refusing to make it earlier. Every step was gated on evidence - byte equality, or a live
ticket that the blueprint names itself - and the three legacy-pointer tickets were corrected rather than satisfied by
moving files into a layout the suite had removed.

READ DURING THE GB-358 SWEEP 2026-11-12: the description reports the post-fix measurement (0 orphans, 0 dangling, against 59 and 50 before), but the command that produces that line was not identifiable from the description and no plan verb performs it - storypole plan has set/step/next/show/collect - so this could not be re-checked the way the other sweep rows were. Name the command in the ticket before closing it.

CLOSED 2026-11-12: the command this ticket never named is `storypole ledger-verify`. Its JSON answer carries a plans block - {"dangling": [], "orphans": []} measured today - and the human output prints a plan blueprints section only when something is wrong, which is why the ticket empty output read as no command existing. Both claims hold: 0 orphans and 0 dangling, against the 59 and 50 recorded before the work. The audit is reported rather than gating (ledger_cmds.rs), so a future orphan is visible without failing a chain, which is the behaviour the description describes.

  TEN WERE DUPLICATES. Resolved through the remint record, each was byte-identical to a blueprint already owned and
  pointed at elsewhere: root plans/BW-3.md and plans/BW-6.md to benchwork's plans/BW-3.md and plans/BW-6.md;
  plans/OF-2.md, plans/GB-48.md and plans/GB-55.md to outfeed's plans/OF-2.md, OF-3.md and OF-6.md; plans/SP-6.md to
  storypole's plans/SP-6.md. The other four were the mirror image - copies sitting in member stores of blueprints owned by
  the harness (benchwork/plans/GB-17.md, benchwork/plans/GB-46.md, chalkline/plans/GB-18.md, storypole/plans/GB-36.md).
  Identical bytes prove no content is lost by keeping one, and the copy removed is always the one whose store does not
  own the ticket.

  TWO WERE UNATTACHED WORK. The two that named tickets alive today - outfeed's OF-23 and joiner's JN-9 - had no plan
  at all - not a stale pointer, an unwritten one. They were adopted with `plan set`, which writes the blueprint into the
  owning store and records it as a `plan_updated` event, so replay serves it; the root copies then became duplicates and
  were removed with the rest.

  `ledger-verify` now reports 0 orphans and 0 dangling pointers. Measured before this work: 59 and 50.

What made the call safe was refusing to make it earlier. Every step was gated on evidence - byte equality, or a live
ticket that the blueprint names itself - and the three legacy-pointer tickets were corrected rather than satisfied by
moving files into a layout the suite had removed.
